cards.title: Wholesale listing check via Other Sellers on Amazon
cards.claim: On an Amazon listing, if filtering 'other sellers on Amazon' by Prime shows four different sellers selling the exact same product, it indicates a wholesale product (not private label) that is allowed to sell on the listing; if no other sellers appear, it indicates only one seller/private label and should not be sold.
cards.action: Open the listing, click 'other sellers on Amazon,' filter by Prime, and count distinct sellers; only proceed if four different sellers sell the exact same product. If no other sellers appear, do not sell on that listing.
applies_when: Evaluating whether an Amazon listing is open to wholesale resale
Checking for private-label listings to avoid
do_not_use_when: The listing shows fewer than four different Prime sellers
There are no other sellers on Amazon for the listing
unknowns: Whether four is a universal threshold or just the speaker's rule
Whether Prime filtering fully captures all sellers
evidence_quotes: you go on the listing and where it says other sellers on Amazon, you click on that and then you're just going to filter by Prime

As long as you see four different sellers selling this exact same product, it means it's a wholesale product, meaning it's a product that is not private label and you're allowed to sell on this listing
if you don't see that at all, then that means there's only one seller on this listing and it's a private label product, meaning I would not recommend you sell that

cards.title: Avoid listings where Amazon is the seller (except Amazon Warehouse)
cards.claim: If Amazon is on the listing, Amazon can sell the product cheaper and is said to win the Buy Box more often because the Buy Box's main component is price; 'Sold by Amazon' should be avoided, while 'Amazon warehouse' is described as Amazon's used products and is fine.
cards.action: Open the Buy Box and check the 'sold by' field; do not sell on the listing if it says just Amazon. If it says Amazon Warehouse, it is treated as used and is fine.
applies_when: Evaluating a listing before choosing to sell on it
Checking whether Amazon itself is a competing seller on the Buy Box
do_not_use_when: The seller field says Amazon Warehouse (described as used products)
The listing has no Amazon seller presence
unknowns: Whether Amazon always wins the Buy Box in every case
Whether the price difference quoted generalizes
evidence_quotes: make sure Amazon is not on the listing
Because if Amazon's on the listing, my friend, you are never going to win on Amazon because Amazon will sell the product cheaper than you
you just open the buy box and then you just check sold by should not say Amazon at all
If it says Amazon warehouse, it's fine because Amazon warehouse is Amazon's used products
So used is fine, but if it's just Amazon, stay away from it

cards.title: Minimum 30% ROI check with VAT on Amazon fees
cards.claim: The last check is minimum 30% ROI; calculate ROI as profit divided by cost of goods multiplied by 100, using the Amazon seller calculator and inputting the ASIN, selling price (matching the lowest seller in the listing is recommended), and cost of goods. Amazon charges 20% VAT on Amazon fees and fulfillment cost, which should be accounted for. The speaker allows adjusting to 20% ROI if the product sells really well, like 2,000 times.
cards.action: Use the Amazon seller calculator with the ASIN, enter the price and cost of goods, account for 20% VAT on Amazon fees and fulfillment, calculate ROI as profit / cost of goods * 100, and require minimum 30% ROI; only consider 20% ROI if the product sells really well, like 2,000 times.
applies_when: Evaluating product profitability for FBA wholesale
Calculating ROI with Amazon fees and VAT
do_not_use_when: ROI is below 30% and the product is not selling really well like 2,000 times
The calculation does not include the stated 20% VAT on fees and fulfillment

Whether the hidden VAT amount is £1.20 or £120 as transcribed
Whether 2,000 sales is the exact threshold for relaxing ROI
evidence_quotes: The last check is to make sure the product has minimum 30% ROI
I recommend you match the price with the lowest seller in the listing
there is a hidden fee on your Amazon fees and your fulfillment cost, which is 20% VAT that is charged on this
Amazon does charge you 20% VAT on the fees or any cost that is seen here
remember the formula for ROI is profit divided by cost of goods multiply by 100
So this is 21% ROI only which does not pass our check of minimum 30% ROI
The only one that I would say you can adjust is the ROI. Sometimes if the product is selling really well, like 2,000 times, I would still go with 20% ROI
